# Code Review — 2026-08-06 (symaira-corekit)

Scope: `main` @ 4d218fe — focus on packages added or changed since the 2026-06-22 review (`domkit` new in #90, `embedkit` #85/#86/#88/#89, `ollamakit` #80, `vectorkit/turboquant`, `evidencekit`). Evidence: package sources, tests, `go.mod`, CI workflow, coverage profile. All three findings of the 2026-06-22 review are verified fixed (sqlitekit DSN pragmas, govulncheck pinned @v1.4.0, `ValidatePath` rejects all control chars). `embedkit` (cache/provider/dimension) is clean: concurrency-safe LRU with defensive vector clones, deterministic fallback that cannot be conflated with a real model. `go vet`, `gofmt`, and `go mod tidy -diff` were run; vet and gofmt are clean, tidy is not (see separate PR).

- [ ] **[Performance] domkit `Render` parses the page up to 3×**
  - **Status quo:** `domkit/schema.go:81` (`Render`) calls `Lang(source)` (parses in `domkit/markdown.go:59`), `schemaTypeFromHTML(source)` (parses in `domkit/schema.go:248`), and `Markdown(source)` (parses in `domkit/markdown.go:38`) — each runs `html.Parse` over the full page. With `Options.Selector`/`Filter` set, `selectSource` parses a fourth time (`domkit/schema.go:126`). For a pipeline whose purpose is rendering large pages for LLM consumption, that is 3–4 full tree builds per read.
  - **Proposed solution:** Parse once in `Render` and pass the `*html.Node` tree through `Lang`, `schemaTypeFromHTML`, `Outline`, `Markdown`, and `selectSource`; keep the string signatures as thin wrappers for API compatibility (or convert to tree-based internals with exported funcs unchanged).
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / medium impact (read latency on large pages).

- [ ] **[UX/DX] domkit attribute selectors deviate from CSS presence semantics**
  - **Status quo:** `matchesAttributeSelector` (`domkit/schema.go:216-233`) treats `[attr]` as "attribute present with a non-empty value" — `value == ""` returns false, so `[data-x]` fails to match `<div data-x="">` where CSS would match on presence. `matchesSelector` splits the selector on whitespace (`domkit/schema.go:185`), so quoted values containing spaces (`[title="a b"]`) break, and values are not unescaped. Consumers using the documented selector subset get silent no-matches on valid HTML.
  - **Proposed solution:** For bare `[attr]`, test attribute presence (iterate `node.Attr` keys), not value non-emptiness; parse `[attr="value with spaces"]` respecting quotes instead of `strings.Fields`; trim `"`/`'` only as a delimiter, not content.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact.

- [ ] **[UX/DX] Broken doc reference `docs/output-schema.md`**
  - **Status quo:** `domkit/schema.go:53` comment says "see `testdata/fetch-schema.json` and `docs/output-schema.md`"; the latter does not exist in this repo (only `docs/cross-language-conventions.md` and `docs/migrations.md`). The JSON-LD/frontmatter contract is documented by `testdata/fetch-schema.json`, so the output-schema pointer is dangling.
  - **Proposed solution:** Point the comment to the actual file (e.g. `testdata/fetch-schema.json`) or to the symfetch/symbrowse repo URL where the schema doc lives.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / low impact.

## Notes

- `go.mod` is stale: `golang.org/x/net` and `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` are imported directly (domkit, configkit) but marked `// indirect`; `go mod tidy -diff` shows the required move. Fixed via PR (separate from this review).
- `vectorkit/turboquant` benchmark tests (`TestBenchmark*`) assert nothing by design (perf smoke); roundtrip tests assert via the shared `testRoundtrip` helper — not a coverage concern.

## Conclusion

The codebase is in good shape; the highest-impact quick win is the domkit single-parse refactor (Performance), which also pays off for symfetch/symbrowse consumers once they migrate to this package (issue #87 tracks that migration).
